dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Looks like there's another painting over here...

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: Aha, very sharp.

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: A bunch of youngsters calling themselves heirs of the Guhua Clan once commissioned Castiglione to paint it. They claim it's their prized "training ground."

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: But they're an awfully proud lot. Think themselves peerless masters already, far above such basic drills. So they handed the painting off to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... Aren't you with the Guhua Clan?

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: Well, I'd love to claim that. Alas, that lad Guhua probably wouldn't dare take me in.

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: Back when we were clearing out bandits at Guili Plains, the boy nearly got himself killed for lack of proper training. I had no choice but to...

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: Ah, never mind. Old, uninteresting business. Though this painting, now... that's another matter.

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: If you're curious, go on and unroll it. No great loss if you tear it — Castiglione's idle most days anyway. I'll have him paint another.

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: Heh... No matter how many times I see it, it still makes no sense to me. I've never heard of anyone honing their swordsmanship by chopping bamboo. That lad Guhua really did have some strange ideas in that head of his.

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: Bamboo can be woven into baskets, carved into slips, shaped into flutes or tally rods, even made into writing brushes. But using it as stakes or training weapons? Now that's a new one. Quite the innovation, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: Alright then, you two! Since the scroll has been unrolled, I'll speak on behalf of those little Guhua Clan disciples and lay out the rules.

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: Among these bamboo dummies, some are <color=#00E1FFFF>dressed in blue</color> while others are <color=#FF5E41FF>dressed in red</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: The first stage of this trial is simple: strike the ones in <color=#00E1FFFF>blue</color>, and do not hit the ones in <color=#FF5E41FF>red</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: If you're ready, you may begin at any time. Let me witness the sharpness of your blade.

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: Excellent! That's a wrap!

dialogues.speaker: Jinggui
dialogues.text: Thank you both, that was a real delight. Your skills are truly impressive, blond youngster. I daresay you're far stronger than that kid Guhua.

response.speaker: Jinggui
response.text: Thanks to the two of you, I've had a rare moment of insight myself. Fish paste really does need a bit of freshly minced meat mixed in to bring out the flavor. Leave it too long, and there's no masking the fishiness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, fair point... Hmm? Wait... that doesn't seem related at all, does it!?

response.speaker: Jinggui
response.text: Haha, never mind such trifles! Next time I have Castiglione paint me a few more fish, I'll treat you both to some proper fish paste!

response.speaker: Jinggui
response.text: No need to be modest. Your swordplay is strong — that much I can tell.

choices.text: Oh, like those at Wangshan Hall...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon remembered too! We have to attack the dummies <color=#00E1FFFF>in blue</color> without hitting a single dummy <color=#FF5E41FF>in red</color>, right?

response.speaker: Jinggui
response.text: Exactly. In that case, I won't waste any more breath. Show me what your sword can do!
